ai.title: Structured session failure replaces plain error string
ai.summary: The freebuff session store now holds a `FreebuffSessionFailure` object instead of a plain error string, carrying a retry field with an absolute timestamp and attempt number, an outcomeUnknown flag for POSTs whose response was lost, and a type discriminator for http, timeout, or other failures. A new `classifyFreebuffSessionRequestFailure` function decides whether a failed session request should retry, stop, or treat the outcome as unknown, retrying only the documented pre-database 503 POST response for POSTs while GETs retry on 408, 429, and 5xx. The landing screen's `TakeoverPrompt` consumes this failure to display scheduled-retry countdown text and distinct messaging for ambiguous outcomes.
ai.evidence: The diff replaces the `error` slot in `useFreebuffSessionStore` with a structured failure type defined as `FreebuffSessionFailure` (cli/src/state/freebuff-session-store.ts) and threads it through app.tsx, freebuff-landing-screen.tsx, and use-freebuff-session.ts. New exports `FreebuffSessionFailure`, `FreebuffSessionRetry`, `classifyFreebuffSessionRequestFailure`, and `isFreebuffSessionTimeoutError` are added to cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-api.ts, and `TakeoverPrompt` now accepts a failure prop to render retry countdowns and outcome-unknown messaging.

ai.title: Windows terminal watchdog opt-in env var and gating logic
ai.summary: Added the `CODEBUFF_ENABLE_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG` env var to `CliEnv` and `getCliEnv()`, and `terminal-watchdog.ts` now refuses to spawn the PowerShell watchdog on Windows unless that variable is truthy, after still honoring `CODEBUFF_NO_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG`. The previous behavior on Windows was to always avoid the watchdog unless `CODEBUFF_NO_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG` was unset, relying on EDR/AV avoidance; the change makes the opt-in explicit so targeted CI and debugging can enable it while keeping the default off. `startTerminalWatchdog`'s `isOptedOut` helper was generalized to `isTruthy` and now checks both flags, and the Windows smoke test no longer injects `CODEBUFF_NO_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG: '1'`, instead deleting both watchdog flags to inherit the parent environment.

eli5.text: When the terminal watchdog tool kills a frozen program with the strongest shutdown signal, the test now waits until the program writes its exact recovery password text to the terminal before declaring victory, rather than stopping as soon as anything appears. The waiting period now matches your operating system: Windows gets up to 45 seconds because it takes longer to wake up and write, while Mac and Linux get 15 seconds, and the overall test timeout grew to two minutes to reduce false failures under heavy load. entries.summary: CLI, Docs changes across 4 file(s) (+175/−78).

ai.title: Terminal broker replaces Windows stdio pipes with temp file
ai.summary: The terminal command broker on Windows no longer relies on Bun's custom fd 3/4 stdio pipes, which could crash the CLI as an unhandled rejection when their node:net handshake failed, and instead writes the broker result to a one-shot temp file (PROTOCOL_FILE_PREFIX='freebuff-terminal-command-broker-') read back by the parent after child close. Parent liveness is now detected by polling the parent PID instead of holding another private socket, and the broker failure message trimmed to 'Restart Freebuff and try again.'. The Windows smoke test doubles its acceptance deadline to 120_000 ms and exercises 64 repeated packaged-broker spawns after the time-sensitive report injection, while docs/agents-and-tools.md documents the console-free, file-based completion protocol.
ai.evidence: cli/src/utils/terminal-command-broker.ts: writeProtocol, waitForParentDisconnect, and createTerminalCommandBroker were rewritten to drop the custom fd 3/4 stdio pipes; instead the broker now writes a one-shot JSON response to a constrained temp file (PROTOCOL_FILE_PREFIX='freebuff-terminal-command-broker-', via protocolPathFromEnv and writeFileSync with flag 'wx') and polls the parent PID; cli/scripts/smoke-terminal-broker-windows.ts: TIMEOUT_MS 60_000->120_000 and added a 64-iteration repeated-broker-spawn loop; cli/src/smoke/terminal-command-broker.ts: added repeatedCommands result field, the 64-iteration repeated command loop, and relaxed the broker-failure assertion to check only 'Restart Freebuff'; docs/agents-and-tools.md: documented the console-free, file-based completion protocol.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the rollout to non-Windows platforms or whether the old fd 3/4 code path was removed entirely versus kept behind a platform check.

changes.what: Removed the custom fd 3/4 stdio pipes and replaced writeProtocol, waitForParentDisconnect, and the completion path with a one-shot temp file written with flag 'wx' and a parent-PID polling loop.
Added a repeatedCommands result field and a 64-iteration repeated-broker-spawn loop, and relaxed the broker-failure assertion to require only 'Restart Freebuff' in the message.
Raised the acceptance deadline from TIMEOUT_MS 60_000 to 120_000 and tightened the OK log line to mention repeated broker spawns.
Documented that the detached helper uses only the three standard stdio channels and reports completion through a constrained one-shot temp file in the OS temp directory.

ai.title: Terminal broker failure telemetry
ai.summary: Added `TERMINAL_BROKER_SPAWN_FAILED` analytics event and `classifyTerminalBrokerFailure` to `terminal-command-broker.ts`. Telemetry fires only on Windows in interactive parent, loading analytics lazily to avoid detached broker side effects. Event added to `ALWAYS_TRACK_EVENTS` in `analytics-sampling.ts` to prevent sampling distortion for rare regressions. Includes `sanitizeTerminalBrokerVersion` to validate version strings before reporting.

eli5.text: When the terminal connection helper fails to start on Windows, the app now silently records that specific failure so the team can spot Windows-only regressions later; it does not change what you see or do when running a command. The recording only happens in the interactive window you type in, and only on the rare spawn failure, so it never slows down normal work or affects the detached background helper. If you noticed nothing different but a Windows-only crash stopped working, that crash is now the kind of error the team can track per software version without being blurred by sampling.
